from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
# Define transform for regular tiled frame/pattern + colored shape layout.
source = '''def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The frame is the uniform-color panel at the left; its perimeter marks tiles.
    frame = grid[0][0]
    left_w = next((c for c in range(1, w) if grid[0][c] != frame), w)
    top_h = next((r for r in range(1, h) if grid[r][0] != frame), h)
    # Determine tile spacing from repeated full frame lines/columns.
    row_bounds = [r for r in range(h) if all(v == frame for v in grid[r][:left_w])]
    col_bounds = [c for c in range(left_w) if all(grid[r][c] == frame for r in range(h))]
    # Grid boundary rows/cols form the regular frame; interior runs are between them.
    row_starts = [r for r in row_bounds if r == 0 or r - 1 not in row_bounds]
    col_starts = [c for c in col_bounds if c == 0 or c - 1 not in col_bounds]
    # For these puzzles the horizontal and vertical frame separators are one-cell thick.
    row_seps = [r for r in row_bounds if r == 0 or r == h - 1 or (r > 0 and r - 1 not in row_bounds)]
    # Use the observed regular panel size: first non-border row after row 0, and first non-frame col.
    rh = next((r for r in range(1, h) if not all(v == frame for v in grid[r][:left_w])), h)
    ch = next((c for c in range(1, left_w) if any(grid[r][c] != frame for r in range(h))), left_w)
    # Boundaries are frame-colored rows/columns; collect their starts.
    rsep = [r for r in range(h) if all(v == frame for v in grid[r][:left_w])]
    csep = [c for c in range(left_w) if all(grid[r][c] == frame for r in range(h))]
    r0s = [0] + [r for r in rsep if r > 0 and r - 1 not in rsep]
    c0s = [0] + [c for c in csep if c > 0 and c - 1 not in csep]
    # Since separators are single lines, panels lie between consecutive separator rows/cols.
    r_edges = sorted(set(rsep + [h]))
    c_edges = sorted(set(csep + [left_w]))
    # Identify all colored components to the right, using 4-neighbor connectivity.
    seen = set()
    shapes = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(left_w, w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color == 0 or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]; seen.add((r, c)); cells = []
            while stack:
                y, x = stack.pop(); cells.append((y, x))
                for yy, xx in ((y-1,x),(y+1,x),(y,x-1),(y,x+1)):
                    if 0 <= yy < h and left_w <= xx < w and (yy,xx) not in seen and grid[yy][xx] == color:
                        seen.add((yy,xx)); stack.append((yy,xx))
            minr = min(y for y,x in cells); minc = min(x for y,x in cells)
            mask = frozenset((y-minr,x-minc) for y,x in cells)
            shapes.append((color, mask))
    out = [row[:left_w] for row in grid]
    # For each framed cell, replace its blank pattern cells with the matching object color.
    # Use the frame separator runs to get each tile interior.
    hsep = [r for r in range(h) if all(v == frame for v in grid[r][:left_w])]
    starts = [r for r in hsep if r == 0 or r-1 not in hsep]
    for i, top in enumerate(starts):
        bottom = next((r for r in hsep if r > top), h)
        rlo, rhi = top + 1, bottom
        if rlo >= rhi: continue
        # left/right vertical frame columns are all-frame; interior lies between them
        vcols = [c for c in range(left_w) if all(grid[r][c] == frame for r in range(h))]
        left = min(vcols); right = max(vcols)
        pattern = frozenset((r-rlo,c-left-1) for r in range(rlo,rhi) for c in range(left+1,right) if grid[r][c] == 0)
        if not pattern: continue
        # normalize mask coordinates; compare exact shape within the tile dimensions
        def norm(cells):
            a=min(r for r,c in cells); b=min(c for r,c in cells)
            return frozenset((r-a,c-b) for r,c in cells)
        match = next((color for color, mask in shapes if mask == norm(pattern)), None)
        if match is not None:
            for r in range(rlo,rhi):
                for c in range(left+1,right):
                    if grid[r][c] == 0: out[r][c] = match
    return out
'''
